mem.t: Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.

lessons.title: Our Father in Heaven
lessons.theme: Prayer begins with knowing the Father and coming to him

v: Therefore don’t be like them, for your Father knows what things you need before you ask him.
Pray like this: “‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.
For you didn’t receive the spirit of bondage again to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry, “Abba! Father!”

lessons.still: Become still and call softly, “Abba, Father.” Repeat it a few times, letting those words settle slowly into your heart. Picture yourself walking into your father’s room like a child—no appointment needed, no speech to prepare.
teach: When children ask their dad for something, they never prepare an eloquent speech first; they simply call out, “Dad!” Many people are afraid to pray because they imagine prayer as addressing a distant authority: the words must be beautiful and it must go on long enough. In teaching us to pray, Jesus tears down that misunderstanding with the very first line.

Jesus says not to pile up empty repetitions like the pagans, because “your Father knows what things you need, before you ask him.” Prayer is not informing God of something he doesn’t know; it is fellowship between children and their Father. “Our Father in heaven”—“our” reminds us we never pray alone; “in heaven” reminds us he is Most High; “Father” reminds us he is nearest and dearest.

Paul says that we did not receive a spirit of slavery but the Spirit of adoption as sons, so we cry, “Abba! Father!” This is the cry the Holy Spirit raises within us. Our mindset must change: I do not earn the right to be a child by praying; I can pray because I am already a child.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The order of relationships—God comes first. Prayer is first of all a relationship, not a tool. The heart of a slave is the self-ruled life, trading performance for rewards; the heart of a son is the self-emptied life, resting in the Father’s love. The Lord’s Prayer is the blueprint for building what belongs to God, and it all begins with “Father.”
q: Who is God? — How does “your Father knows” change the way you see prayer?
Who am I? — When you pray, are you more like a servant giving a report or a child talking to their father?
How shall I respond? — How will you speak to the Father like a child today?
lessons.jesus: In his most agonising hour in Gethsemane, Jesus still cried, “Abba, Father.” He is God’s only Son, with an eternal, intimate relationship with the Father; through the cross he shares that relationship with us, so that we too can call God Father.
lessons.pray: Abba, heavenly Father, thank you that I am no longer a slave but your child. I don’t need beautiful words; you already know what I need. Today I come before you like a child, open my heart to you, and rest in your love. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: As you pray today, begin with “Abba, Father” and simply say three things that are on your heart
Write down one way the heavenly Father has cared for you, and thank him specifically
When praying for a friend, say “our Father,” remembering that you are family
lessons.noon: “For your Father knows what things you need before you ask him.” — Lord, my Father, right now I rest and rely on you.

lessons.title: May Your Name Be Kept Holy
lessons.theme: Prayer cares first about God’s name, not mine

v: In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up; and his train filled the temple.
Above him stood the seraphim. Each one had six wings. With two he covered his face. With two he covered his feet. With two he flew.
One called to another, and said, “Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of Armies! The whole earth is full of his glory!”

lessons.still: Close your eyes and picture the throne and the seraphim Isaiah saw. Today, don’t rush to ask for anything; just say softly three times, “Holy, holy, holy.” Let God’s greatness fill your heart first, and then begin to pray.
teach: A telescope brings a distant planet near and magnifies it. It doesn’t actually make the planet bigger; it lets us see how big it really is. “Hallowing God’s name” is like that: we cannot make God any holier, but we can “magnify” his holiness in our lives so that others see the greatness he truly has.

Isaiah saw the Lord in the year King Uzziah died—the earthly throne stood empty, but the Lord still sat on the heavenly throne. The seraphim covered their faces and feet with their wings and cried, “Holy!” “Holy” means set apart, transcendent, and perfectly pure. The first petition of the Lord’s Prayer is not for ourselves but for God’s name.

Our prayers often look like a shopping list centred on “me.” Jesus reverses the order: first God’s name, God’s kingdom and God’s will, and only then our needs. This doesn’t mean our needs are unimportant; rather, when God is put first, everything else finds its proper place.
lessons.light: 321 Light: One of the two core values—let Jesus receive all the glory. “Hallowing his name” means not stealing God’s glory. Self-ruled people are like the builders of Babel, wanting to “make a name for ourselves”; self-emptied people want only God’s name to be lifted high.
q: Who is God? — The seraphim cover their faces and cry “Holy”; what does this show you of God’s majesty?
Who am I? — In your prayers, how much is for God’s name and how much for your own needs?
How shall I respond? — In what situation today could you lead people to honour God because of you?
lessons.jesus: In his prayer before he was betrayed, Jesus said, “I glorified you on the earth. I have accomplished the work which you have given me to do.” The goal of his whole life was to glorify the Father’s name. He also prayed for us, that we would likewise make the Father’s name known in the world.
lessons.pray: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Armies! The whole earth is full of your glory. I confess that my prayers are often centred on myself. Today, first of all, I ask that your name be kept holy and lifted high in my words, my work and my family. May all glory go to you, not to me. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: For the first three minutes of your prayer today, only praise God—make no requests
Before each task, pray silently: “May your name be kept holy here”
Turn something you were praised for into a testimony of God’s grace
lessons.noon: “Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of Armies!” — Lord, right now may your name be kept holy in me.

lessons.title: Let Your Kingdom Come
lessons.theme: Letting God reign is the most fundamental prayer

v: Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.
He went forward a little, fell on his face, and prayed, saying, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass away from me; nevertheless, not what I desire, but what you desire.”

lessons.still: Hold in your heart the one thing you care about most today. Quietly lift it before the Lord and say, “Lord, in this matter, let your kingdom come and let your will be done.” Then slowly open your hands.
teach: You can tell a nation’s territory by where its flag is planted. God’s kingdom is not a geographical territory but wherever God reigns as King. When I pray, “Let your Kingdom come,” I am saying, “Lord, plant your flag in my home, my work and my heart.”

“Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven”—just as the angels in heaven obey immediately, joyfully and completely, may it be so on earth. The truest demonstration of this line is in Gethsemane: sorrowful almost to death, Jesus still said, “Not what I desire, but what you desire.” God’s kingdom often comes when “what I desire” steps down from the throne.

This is this week’s memory verse and the heart of the Lord’s Prayer. It contains an exchange: laying down my kingdom and welcoming God’s. At first it may feel like a loss, but God’s will is always good, perfect and pleasing. Letting God reign is not a loss but a return to the very best plan.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The two core values—let Jesus reign; let Jesus receive all the glory. Building what belongs to God means fulfilling the Lord’s Prayer: his will done on earth as it is in heaven. Every time we say “not what I desire,” we lay one more brick in God’s kingdom system.
q: Who is God? — What does it mean for your life that God’s will is perfectly done in heaven?
Who am I? — In what matter is your prayer really “Let my kingdom come”?
How shall I respond? — In which decision today will you say, “What you desire”?
lessons.jesus: The first words of Jesus’ preaching were, “Repent, for the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand.” Wherever he went, the sick were healed, demons were driven out and sins were forgiven—God’s kingdom came in him. In Gethsemane he surrendered his will entirely to the Father, and the cross became the road to the kingdom’s victory.
lessons.pray: Heavenly Father, let your kingdom come; let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven. I place my home, my work and my plans before you. Not what I desire, but what you desire. Reign in every corner of my life. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Before making a decision, pray first: “What you desire”
At home or at work, find one matter where you deliberately put God’s heart first
lessons.noon: “Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth.” — Lord, right now please reign here.

lessons.title: Today’s Bread and Forgiveness
lessons.theme: Relying on God’s provision daily, and living out forgiveness daily

v: Give us today our daily bread.
Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.
“For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
But if you don’t forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.

lessons.still: Quietly thank the Lord for what you need today: food, strength, wisdom. Then ask the Holy Spirit to bring a name to mind—someone you still can’t let go of. You don’t need to resolve it right away; simply bring that person honestly before the Lord.
teach: In the wilderness the Israelites gathered manna every morning, only enough for that day; if they kept extra until the next day, it bred worms and stank. God was training them to depend on him day by day. “Give us today our daily bread” is likewise an invitation to live a life of trust one day at a time, not carrying tomorrow’s worries into today.

Right after it comes, “Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.” Of all the lines in the Lord’s Prayer, this is the only one Jesus went on to explain. This does not mean forgiving others is the price of salvation; it means that those who have truly received great forgiveness will inevitably let forgiveness flow out. Refusing to forgive shows that the door of the heart has closed to grace as well.

It is no accident that bread and forgiveness sit side by side: the body needs daily bread, and relationships need daily forgiveness. Unforgiveness is like drinking poison yourself and waiting for the other person to collapse. Forgiveness is not pretending nothing happened, nor is it instantly restoring trust; it is handing the right to judge back to God, and no longer letting bitterness reign in our hearts.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The order of relationships—first with God, then with ourselves, then with others. Only when we receive forgiveness from God do we have the strength to forgive others. Pride says, “I have the right to hold a grudge”; humility lays down that power and lets God be the Judge. People matter more than things; don’t hurt people for the sake of things.
q: Who is God? — God provides every day and forgives every day; what does this show you of his abundance?
Who am I? — Are you still clutching some “debt” that someone owes you?
How shall I respond? — Whose name will you hand over to God today, to begin the journey of forgiveness?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said, “I am the bread of life.” He doesn’t just provide food; he himself is the bread of life. On the cross he prayed for those who crucified him: “Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing.” With his own body he accomplished the provision and the forgiveness we need.
lessons.pray: Heavenly Father, thank you for providing for my needs every day. Give me today my daily bread, and teach me to rely on you one day at a time. Thank you, too, for forgiving my enormous debt. Help me to forgive those who have hurt me, to hand judgement over to you, and not to let bitterness reign in my heart. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Before each meal, thank God specifically for one provision
Write down a name you need to forgive, and pray one sentence of blessing over that person
Today, stop bringing up one way someone wronged you in the past
lessons.noon: “Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.” — Lord, right now I hand judgement over to you.

lessons.title: Yours Is the Kingdom, the Power and the Glory
lessons.theme: Prayer begins with worship and ends with worship

v: Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory forever. Amen.’

Yours, LORD, is the greatness, the power, the glory, the victory, and the majesty! For all that is in the heavens and on the earth is yours. Yours is the kingdom, LORD, and you are exalted as head above all.

lessons.still: Quietly recall what you have prayed about this week. Then open your hands, palms upward, and declare, “Yours is the kingdom, the power and the glory.” Let these words seal all your requests like a stamp.
teach: The signature at the end of a letter determines the weight of the whole letter. The Lord’s Prayer closes with “yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory,” which is like stamping a seal on every request: all of this belongs to God and is accomplished by God. This ending keeps prayer centred on God from beginning to end.

“Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one”—we admit that we are weak and need God’s protection. Then the prayer turns to praise. After David gathered offerings to prepare for building the temple, he praised God in the same way: “Yours, Yahweh, is the greatness, the power, the glory, the victory, and the majesty!” The people had given much, yet they confessed that everything belonged to God to begin with.

This week we have walked through the Lord’s Prayer: knowing the Father, hallowing his name, letting God reign, relying on his provision and living out forgiveness, and finally giving the glory to God. Building what belongs to God means fulfilling the Lord’s Prayer. Next week we will go deeper into a key truth: for God’s kingdom to come, we must first return to our place—humility.
lessons.light: 321 Light: One purpose—building what belongs to God means giving the kingdom, the power and the glory entirely to God. Self-ruled people want a share of the pie, keeping a little power and a little glory for themselves; self-emptied people gladly give it all to the Lord. Giving glory to God and thanks in everything is the destination of the path of service.
q: Who is God? — “All that is in the heavens and in the earth is yours”: how does this shape the way you view everything you own?
Who am I? — What portion of power or glory are you secretly trying to keep for yourself?
How shall I respond? — When you finish a task today, how will you give the glory to God?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus was tempted, Satan offered him the glory of all the kingdoms of the world if only he would bow down and worship. Jesus refused that shortcut and chose the cross. After his resurrection he said, “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.” He walked the road of humility and received the true kingdom and glory.
lessons.pray: Lord, yours is the kingdom, the power and the glory forever. Everything I have comes from you, and everything I accomplish is your grace. Deliver me from the evil one, and take away the pride in my heart that wants a share of your glory. May I live my whole life only for your kingdom and your glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Pray through the whole Lord’s Prayer once in your own words
Each time you finish a task today, pray silently: “Glory to you”
At the weekend, pray the Lord’s Prayer together with a spiritual companion
lessons.noon: “For yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory forever.” — Lord, right now all glory goes to you.
